From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Health  SOC 2 & retention requirements  Post-call recap

Hi Alice  thanks again for taking the time today. Really appreciate the candid conversation about Acme Health's security and data-retention needs. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps.

Key pain points you shared
- Need for SOC 2 Type II evidence and recent pen test artifacts for procurement.
- Audit/log retention policy: legal expects up to 5+ years for certain records; you asked about options for 7 years.
- Requirement to forward logs to your security team (Splunk/Syslog) and to control retention lifecycle (S3, archive).
- Data processing terms: DPA redlines and encryption-at-rest/KMS controls.

What we heard as goals
1) Submit SOC 2 + pen-test summary to procurement within 10 business days.
2) Confirm log export capabilities and retention approach that meet your audit needs.
3) Align on deployment option  Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private  based on data residency and retention SLAs.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- SOC 2 Type II report (we'll attach the recent report and a pen-test executive summary).
- We support syslog/S3 export, and Dedicated/Private deployments can provide extended archive retention windows.
- Standard DPA available; we can iterate on specific redlines you surface.

Proposed next steps
1) I will attach the SOC 2 summary, pen-test executive summary, and a sample DPA (attached). Please review and confirm receipt.
2) Can you confirm whether Splunk forwarding (syslog) or S3 export is required for your security team?
3) Suggest scheduling a short 30-min call next week with our security engineer (Rishi) and solutions engineer to go over log formats, retention mechanics, and DPA items. Options: Wed 2027-05-12 10:00 PT or Thu 2027-05-13 09:00 PT.

Please let me know which slot works or propose alternatives. If procurement has a PO timeline or specific checklist items, send them over and we'll prioritize.

Thanks  looking forward to moving this forward.

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa  that recap is helpful and aligns with what I captured. A few follow-ups from procurement/security: 

1) Can you confirm the pen-test vendor (name) and whether we can get an attest/summary suitable for procurement review? Full reports are often redacted; a signed executive summary is acceptable.
2) We need concrete confirmation on log-forwarding: does Redwood support real-time syslog to Splunk (UDP/TCP) or scheduled S3 export? Any limitations on retention windows for hosted customers?
3) On the DPA side, we'll likely redline a few sections around subprocessor lists and data retention. Can you share the current subprocessor list and a recommended contact for legal to work with?

Timeline: procurement needs docs by end of next week (2027-05-16) to keep our Q2 timeline. Also confirming internal: Bob (cc'd) will own procurement and will follow-up with PO questions.

If you can get the SOC2 summary and pen-test exec summary by EOD tomorrow, that would keep us on track. The follow-up call with your security engineer would be great  Wed 5/12 10:00 PT should work; I'll confirm calendar.

Best,
Alice

Marissa/Neha  quick internal note with answers to the specific questions Alice raised: 

- Pen-test vendor: SecureOps. We run an annual third-party assessment; SecureOps provides an exec summary and a redacted report. We can produce a signed attestation/executive summary suitable for procurement.
- SOC 2: Type II report (covering 2026 audit period) is available. We can share the report under an NDA/secure link.
- Log forwarding: Redwood supports both real-time syslog (TCP/UDP) to customer endpoints and S3 export. For Hosted customers, retention is typically 90-365 days; Dedicated/Private customers can configure extended archive retention (we support archive to S3 with lifecycle rules and can retain up to 7 years if required by contract).
- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list; Neha can export the current list and attach.
- Encryption/KMS: BYOK is supported on Dedicated/Private via customer-managed KMS; Hosted customers get platform-managed encryption with options for Bring-Your-Own-Key on enterprise tier.

Attachments I will push to the thread: SOC2-Report-Redwood-2026.pdf (redacted stub), PenTest-Summary-Redwood-SecureOps-2026.pdf (stub).

Recommend: include a short SE session to review log format (CEF/JSON), Splunk connector, and retention SLAs. I'm available Wed 5/12 10:00 PT.

Rishi
